Class SpringConfigurationPostProcessor

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.config.SpringConfigurationPostProcessor
All Implemented Interfaces:
EventListener, ApplicationListener<ContextRefreshedEvent>
@Deprecated(since="6.0.0", forRemoval=true) public class SpringConfigurationPostProcessor extends Object implements ApplicationListener<ContextRefreshedEvent>
Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
the holders and registrars that used to be filled by this listener now collect their own contributions, so this bean can simply be removed from the application context. Running on a ContextRefreshedEvent was also too late: every singleton has been created by then, so anything resolving e.g. a mapping during bean initialization saw an empty MappingService. See SpringBidiMappingService, SpringDynamicExtensionRegistrar, org.openehealth.ipf.modules.hl7.config.CustomModelClassesRegistrar and org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.core.config.CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer.

Note that this listener also created a SpringRegistry as a side effect, and thereby initialized the ContextFacade that the stateful Groovy and Kotlin extensions look up beans in. Contexts that relied on that side effect have to declare the registry explicitly when dropping this bean: 

    <ipf:globalContext/>
Spring Listener which holds the instances of all OrderedConfigurer. These instances are collected from the Spring context on a ContextRefreshedEvent.
Author:
Boris Stanojevic
